note: One §4.1c mutation per rendered verdict marker. A kill counts only when the unmutated baseline passed in the same run and the failure is that verdict's own assertion. Recorded failures are in the commit body.

tree-point.renders: #tree-verdict — ONE LIT POINT AT α = n
tree-point.computedFrom: evaluateAll(k0) XOR evaluateAll(k1), reading back the lit index
tree-point.mutation: src/dpf/gen.ts — flip every direction bit: ((alpha >>> (domainBits - level - 1)) & 1) becomes (((alpha >>> (domainBits - level - 1)) & 1) ^ 1)
tree-point.expectedFlip: point lands at 15 - α, so data-status becomes alarm and the text becomes POINT AT THE WRONG INDEX

single-share.renders: #collusion-view verdict with the collusion toggle off — ONE KEY ONLY · k0 alone lights n of 16 leaves
single-share.mutation: src/attack/single-view.ts — namesAPoint: lit === 1 becomes namesAPoint: lit >= 1
single-share.expectedFlip: a share lighting ~8 leaves is reported as naming a point, so data-status becomes alarm

collusion-recovery.renders: #collusion-view verdict with the collusion toggle on — SERVER SEES α = n
collusion-recovery.computedFrom: collude(k0, k1).alpha compared with the client's secret α
collusion-recovery.mutation: src/attack/collude.ts — alpha: lit[0][0] becomes alpha: (lit[0][0] + 1) % reconstruction.length
collusion-recovery.expectedFlip: recovered index no longer equals α, so data-status becomes mismatch and the text becomes JOIN MISSED

server-view-0.renders: first #privacy-verdicts tile — Server 0 · one party-0 key of 290 B · folded n of 65,536 records
server-view-0.computedFrom: deserializeKey(keys[0]).party, keys[0].length, and fold0.foldedRecords from the real fold
server-view-0.mutation: src/pir/server.ts — in serverAnswerProgressive, if (share[index] === 0) continue becomes if (share[index] === 0 || index !== 0) continue
server-view-0.expectedFlip: the server folds at most the first record, so folded > 1 fails and data-status becomes alarm

server-view-1.renders: second #privacy-verdicts tile — Server 1 · one party-1 key of 290 B · folded n of 65,536 records
server-view-1.computedFrom: deserializeKey(keys[1]).party, keys[1].length, and fold1.foldedRecords from the real fold
server-view-1.mutation: src/dpf/serialize.ts — bytes[0] = (key.party << 7) | key.domainBits becomes bytes[0] = key.domainBits, dropping the party bit from the wire format
server-view-1.expectedFlip: server 1's key deserializes as party 0, so only this tile's data-status becomes alarm while server-view-0 stays pass

collusion-state.renders: third #privacy-verdicts tile — Collusion is off / Collusion is ON
collusion-state.computedFrom: the live state of #collusion-toggle at fetch time
collusion-state.mutation: src/ui/app.ts — const colluding = element<HTMLInputElement>('collusion-toggle').checked becomes const colluding = false
collusion-state.expectedFlip: a fetch run with collusion switched on still reports the tile as pass

record-match.renders: #record-verdict — RETRIEVED · byte-for-byte match with shelf[α] / RETRIEVED — AND WRONG
record-match.computedFrom: sameBytes(reconstruct(answer0, answer1), shelf[α]) and the differing byte count
record-match.mutation: src/pir/client.ts — reconstruct returns answer0.map((byte, index) => byte ^ (answer1[index] & 0)), dropping server 1 from the XOR
record-match.expectedFlip: the reconstruction no longer equals shelf[alpha], so data-status becomes alarm on the honest run

no-authentication.computedFrom: whether a tampered answer reconstructed to something other than shelf[α] with no error raised
no-authentication.expectedFlip: the tampered run matches shelf[α], so data-status becomes contradicted rather than alarm
